summary: Yutaka Iwamoto worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, and Hidenaka Tanaka. He held posts at Kyoto University, Tokai University (~1968–1974), Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka University.
Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He held an attested post at the University of Tokyo in 2024.

Yutaka Ochihara worked in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947) under Atsuuji Ashikaga and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Louis Renou, and Armand Minard. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986).
Yutaka Takagi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and was a professor at Rissho University (~1966–1999).

Yutaka Yoshida works in history/archaeology, Japanology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018) and Kyoto University (~2006–2020).

Yutaka Yuda worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura and completed studies at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held faculty posts at Kyoritsu University of Pharmacy and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).
Yutang Lin was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at St. John's, Harvard, and Leipzig University under August Conrady. He held a post at Peking University from ~1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura specializes in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2020), Kyoto University as a postdoctoral fellow (2015–2018), and the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

Yuzo Mizoguchi specialized in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, the University of Tokyo (1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Zarawar Khan specializes in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied under Pe Maung Tin at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1929) and later studied at the University of Dublin (~1937–1939).

Zeff Bjerken works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).
Zellig Harris was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held academic posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University (~1946–1947).

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018) and was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Zenjo Inoue was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji.
Zenkei Shibayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Otani University (~1938–1946) and Hanazono University (~1946–1974).
Zenno Ikuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Taisho University. He served as professor and professor emeritus at Taisho University, president of Shukutoku Junior College (2002–2014), and professor at Shukutoku University (2014).

Zennosuke Tsuji worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1938), University of the Sacred Heart (~1948–1955), and Rissho University (~1952–1955).

Zenryu Tsukamoto worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities under scholars including Toru Haneda and Jitsuzo Kuwabara. He served as a professor and president at Kyoto University and director of Kyoto National Museum.
